findings.title: update() takes the 'before' login state from the org-aware wrapper, so a disabled org hides the IDP's old state and the login cache is not invalidated
findings.body:
`update()` gets `idpById` from `getById()` (line 91). `getById()` returns `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel(...)` (lines 135-141), whose `isEnabled()` returns false while the IDP's organization is disabled (lines 436-441). `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` then evaluates `getLoginPredicate()` on that wrapper (lines 405-409), so the IDP reads as not-login.

Failure sequence, using only code this PR touches or calls:
1. Organization O is disabled. IDP X in O is enabled, `BROKER_PUBLIC=true`, not hidden.
2. A login search runs. The JPA `getForLogin` filters only IDP fields, not org state (server-spi IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:165-184), so X's id is cached. On a cache hit the IDs are returned without re-checking `BROKER_PUBLIC` (lines 232-254).
3. An admin sets X to `BROKER_PUBLIC=false`. `original` is the wrapper with `isEnabled()==false`, so both predicates are false and `update()` returns without invalidating (lines 405-407).
4. The admin re-enables O. Org changes register only org keys (model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/organization/InfinispanOrganizationProvider.java:300-315), so the login caches still hold X.
5. The next login search hits the cache. X comes back through `getById` as a wrapper with `isEnabled()==true`. The bean keeps it (services/.../OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java:79-82), so an IDP the admin made non-public is offered on the login page.

Fix: evaluate the 'before' predicate on the stored state, not the org-aware wrapper, e.g. `IdentityProviderModel stored = idpDelegate.getById(model.getInternalId());` and pass `stored` to `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate`. The cache membership is decided from the raw JPA state, and `remove()` already uses the raw `idpDelegate.getByAlias` (line 100) for the same purpose. Keep `getById` for the id/alias invalidation at line 92.
findings.originReason: The update-time login invalidation, which takes the org-aware getById result as 'original', is new in this diff.

verification.reason: `update()` hands the result of `getById` (an org-aware wrapper whose `isEnabled()` is false while the org is disabled) to `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` as the original. So an enabled, public IDP of a disabled org reads as not-login. If the update makes it non-public, both predicates are false and the method returns early, so the cache is not invalidated. The JPA query filters only the IDP's own `enabled` column. Org updates invalidate only org keys, and a cache hit returns the IDs without re-checking `BROKER_PUBLIC`. Once the org is re-enabled, the bean's `isEnabled()` check (lines 79-80) lets the stale IDP through.

findings.title: Cleanup removes the literal alias "alias", so the 21 IDPs created by this test are never removed and later counts depend on method order
findings.body:
The cleanup at line 381 (and line 425) calls `identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` rather than the alias just created. The sibling test copied this pattern at line 303. Nothing is removed, so `idp-alias-0..20` stay in the realm for the rest of the class.

The counts in this test (REALM_ONLY 5/6/5 at lines 404, 486, 522) assume no other realm-level login IDPs. `testCacheIDPByOrg` leaves `org-idp-0..9` behind. `orga`/`orgb` are removed by their own cleanup (test base AbstractOrganizationTest.java:146), and `JpaOrganizationProvider.remove` unlinks every IDP it holds (model/jpa/src/main/java/org/keycloak/organization/jpa/JpaOrganizationProvider.java:141, 358-371). Those leftover IDPs lose their org id and `BROKER_PUBLIC`. If they are enabled, they become realm-level login IDPs, and this test's REALM_ONLY assertions fail when `testCacheIDPByOrg` runs first. I did not verify that the org broker template is enabled, nor the JUnit method order.

Fix: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove);` in the loop, and the matching `"idp-alias-20"` cleanup at line 425. The same literal-alias bug at line 303 should be fixed too.
findings.originReason: Lines 381 and 425 are new in this diff. The same pattern at line 303 is pre-existing (base line 301).

verification.reason: The cleanup removes the literal alias "alias", so none of the `idp-alias-*` IDPs are removed. The realm is not re-imported between methods (`isImportAfterEachMethod` defaults to false), so the IDPs persist through the class. Org removal unlinks its IDPs and strips `BROKER_PUBLIC`. The `org-idp-*` IDPs that `testCacheIDPByOrg` leaves behind therefore become realm-level IDPs and can skew the REALM_ONLY counts, depending on method order.

findings.title: Create and remove of a login-eligible IDP are not covered, and the org-disabled case is not covered
findings.body: Step 1 only creates a hidden IDP (lines 418-425) and removes a disabled one (line 428). Neither path exercises the 'invalidate' branch of `registerIDPLoginInvalidation` for a login-eligible IDP. Nothing checks that creating or removing an org-linked, public IDP clears the login caches. Nothing covers an org that is disabled while its IDP's `BROKER_PUBLIC` changes, which is the path in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:91. Adding those cases would have caught that path.

verification.reason: Step 1 creates only a hidden IDP and removes only a disabled one (`idp-alias-1`). No step creates or removes a login-eligible IDP, and no step updates an IDP while its org is disabled. The invalidating branch of `registerIDPLoginInvalidation` and the org-disabled update path are therefore untested.

findings.title: New org rule in getLoginPredicate also changes the plain IdentityProviderBean's filter for a user's linked IDPs when organizations are disabled
findings.body:
`getLoginPredicate()` is also the default `federatedProviderPredicate()` of the plain `IdentityProviderBean` (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/forms/login/freemarker/model/IdentityProviderBean.java:225-227). That predicate filters the user's linked IDPs at line 213. The plain bean is used when the realm has organizations disabled (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/forms/login/freemarker/FreeMarkerLoginFormsProvider.java:482-486).

Before this PR, a linked IDP that belongs to an org and is not `BROKER_PUBLIC` was still offered in that case. The new `orgId == null || BROKER_PUBLIC` clause removes it. The PR description does not mention this. Is the intent that such a linked IDP should disappear from the login page when organizations are disabled? I did not verify whether an org-linked IDP can exist in a realm with organizations disabled.
findings.originReason: The org/BROKER_PUBLIC clause is added to `getLoginPredicate` by this diff. The base predicate had only nonNull plus the LoginFilter checks.

verification.reason: The plain `IdentityProviderBean` uses `getLoginPredicate()` as `federatedProviderPredicate()` to filter a user's linked IDPs. That bean is used when organizations are disabled for the realm. A linked org IDP that is not `BROKER_PUBLIC` was shown before this change and is now filtered out. This is a valid question about intended behaviour.

findings.title: getForLogin Javadoc omits the public-organization-broker condition that getLoginPredicate now enforces
findings.body: The Javadoc says an IDP can be used for login if it is enabled, not link-only, and not hidden on login (lines 151-152). `getLoginPredicate()` now also requires `organizationId == null || BROKER_PUBLIC` (line 254). The doc should state that IDPs linked to an organization are offered only when `BROKER_PUBLIC` is set, as the ORG_ONLY/ALL paragraph implies but does not say.

verification.reason: The `getForLogin` Javadoc lists only enabled, not link-only and not hidden. The default implementation also requires `BROKER_PUBLIC=true` for org IDPs (line 180), and `getLoginPredicate` now encodes that rule (line 254). The doc does not state this condition.

contracts.action: getForLogin cache path: cached query of IDP ids, then getById per id, for REALM_ONLY/ORG_ONLY/ALL
contracts.before_after: Before: getForLogin used the interface default, which calls getAllStream and wraps each IDP on every call. After: the id set is cached per mode and search key, and the models are re-read through getById, which wraps them. The sibling getByOrganization does the same, minus the org-id invalidation check.
contracts.visible_effect: The login IDP list in the realm page and the org-aware bean (sorted by IDP_COMPARATOR_INSTANCE). Order is not preserved from the HashSet, but the callers sort.
contracts.failure_mode: If getById returns null for a cached id, the key is invalidated and the code falls back to the delegate (lines 246-249). The cache can hold ids whose current BROKER_PUBLIC or enabled state has changed, and the cache-hit path does not re-check the predicate. Correctness therefore depends on update() invalidating correctly (see the update() finding).

contracts.action: update() registers login-cache invalidation from the before and after state
contracts.before_after: Before: update() invalidated only the id and alias keys. After: it also invalidates the three login keys when the login state changes, judged from getById() (org-aware wrapper) as the before-state.
contracts.visible_effect: After an admin edit, the login page shows the new list on the next request. When the before-state is wrong, a stale list stays visible.
contracts.failure_mode: When the org is disabled, the wrapper reports isEnabled()==false for the old state, so an edit that makes the IDP non-public is judged to change nothing. The login cache keeps the id. After the org is re-enabled, the non-public IDP is offered on the login page, because the org re-enable does not invalidate login keys and the cache-hit path returns the IDP through the wrapper.

contracts.action: create() registers login-cache invalidation for the new IDP
contracts.before_after: Before: create() invalidated only the count key. After: it also invalidates the login keys if the new IDP is login-eligible, judged on the raw input model.
contracts.visible_effect: A new public IDP appears on the login page on the next request.
contracts.failure_mode: The predicate is null-safe, and the input model is raw (no org wrapper), so a wrong before-state cannot occur here.

contracts.action: remove() registers login-cache invalidation from the raw stored IDP
contracts.before_after: Before: the stored IDP was read by alias only when the alias key was invalid. After: it is read on every remove (an extra uncached DB read), and the same object feeds both the id/alias invalidation and the login invalidation.
contracts.visible_effect: A removed public IDP disappears from the login page on the next request.
contracts.failure_mode: If the alias does not exist, storedIdp is null. The null check comes first in the predicate (server-spi IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:253), so no NPE is raised. Pre-existing: the isInvalid branch at line 103 still NPEs on null, as it did before.

contracts.action: getLoginPredicate gains an org-public rule, which is also the plain bean's linked-IDP filter
contracts.equivalent_path: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/forms/login/freemarker/model/IdentityProviderBean.java:225-227 (federatedProviderPredicate default) and :209-216 (getFederatedIdentityProviders, which applies it to the user's linked IDPs)
contracts.before_after: Before: the predicate checked enabled, link-only and hide-on-login only. After: it also requires organizationId == null or BROKER_PUBLIC. OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean adds its own org rules on top of super, so the change is redundant there. The plain bean has no such rule, so its behavior changes.
contracts.visible_effect: In a realm with organizations disabled, a user's linked IDP that belongs to an org and is not BROKER_PUBLIC is no longer offered on the login page.
contracts.failure_mode: The user can no longer log in through a linked IDP that they could before. This is silent (no log or error).
contracts.open_question: Can an IDP keep an organization link while the realm has organizations disabled, and if so, should a user's existing link to it still be offered on the login page?

contracts.action: OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean re-checks isEnabled on the cached IDP results
contracts.equivalent_path: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/organization/forms/login/freemarker/model/OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java:58-61 (REALM_ONLY, no re-check, but realm-level IDPs have no org so the wrapper's isEnabled is the raw value)
contracts.before_after: Before: the ORG_ONLY and ALL branches filtered only on alias. After: they also filter on isEnabled(), which for an org-linked IDP also depends on the org being enabled.
contracts.visible_effect: IDPs whose organization is disabled no longer appear on the login page.
contracts.failure_mode: The re-check fixes the disabled-org case but does not repair the stale-cache case in the update() finding, because the cache-hit path does not re-check BROKER_PUBLIC.

summary: The cache design works for the paths the new test covers: org link and unlink go through update(), and create/remove are null-safe. The main defect is in update(): the 'before' login state comes from the org-aware wrapper, so an edit made while the org is disabled can leave a stale login cache that offers a non-public IDP after the org is re-enabled (fix). The new test cleans up by the literal alias "alias", so its IDPs leak and its counts depend on method order (fix, medium confidence). Two smaller points: the getLoginPredicate change also reaches the plain bean's linked-IDP filter in realms without organizations (a question for the author), and the getForLogin Javadoc omits the public-org rule. Nothing was built or run, per the read-only instruction.
